ORAL JUDGMENT 1.
Heard learned Advocate Mr. S.P. Hasurkar for the appellant and learned Advocate Mr. K.M. Sheth for the respondents - claimants.
NEUT  C/FA/1719/2008 JUDGMENT DATED: 19/01/2023
unde 2.

By way of this appeal, the appellant calls into question the judgment and order dated 14.02.2007 passed by the learned Principal Senior Civil Judge, Gandhinagar, in Land Acquisition Reference No.
575 of 1998.

3. It appears that by way of the said decision, the learned Reference Court has awarded an amount of Rs. 100/- per sq. mtr. with regard to the land acquired, with an additional amount of compensation at the rate of 12% on additional compensation along with solatium at the rate of 30%
and further interest on additional compensation at the rate of 9% per annum from the date of taking possession or from the date of issuance of Notification under Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act,
whichever was earlier for the first year, and thereafter at the rate of 15% per annum till realization of the payable aggregate amount according to the provisions of Section 28 of the Land Acquisition Act.
The said decision, being challenged in context of the fact that the Special Land Acquisition Officer had awarded an amount of Rs. 4 per sq. mtr. for the land in question and whereas the appellant,
being also aggrieved by the fact that the learned Reference Court had placed reliance upon an award passed in Reference Nos. 105 of 1997 to 115 of 1997 with regard to a village Alampur where an additional amount of compensation at the rate of Rs. 67 and Rs. 77 per sq. mtr. had been awarded.

The case of the appellant being that the land of village Alampur, NEUTRAL CITATION Executive Engineer (Constru.) vs Manguben Wd/O. Maganbhai Ishwarbhai on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/16942560/
2 C/FA/1719/2008 JUDGMENT DATED: 19/01/2023 undefined was not a comparable instance,
more particularly since the land was situated approximately 11 k.m. a far from the present land.
4.

Heard learned Advocate Mr. S.P. Hasurkar for the appellant and learned Advocate Mr. K.M.
Sheth for the respondents - claimants.

5. Learned Advocate Mr. S.P. Hasurkar would submit that the land in question situated in village Sadara, Taluka and District Gandhinagar, had been acquired for the purpose of 66 K.V. Sub-station and whereas according to learned Advocate Mr. Hasurkar, notice under Section 4(1) and 9(10) of the Land Acquisition Act, had been served upon the claimants.

Learned Advocate would further submit that the Special Land Acquisition Officer had awarded compensation at the rate of Rs. 4 per sq. mtr.
in Land Acquisition Case No. 18 of 1991 and whereas being aggrieved by the same, the claimants had preferred the Reference Case No. 575 of 1998.

Learned Advocate would submit that the learned Reference Court, had inter alia considered a land at village Alampur as being a comparable instance,
for awarding compensation at the rate of Rs. 100/- per sq. mtr. and whereas according to learned Advocate Mr. Hasurkar, the contention of the appellant before the learned Reference Court was that land at village Alampur was not a comparable instance since the land was situated around NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1719/2008 JUDGMENT DATED: 19/01/2023 undefined 11 k.m. from the present land and whereas furthermore, according to learned Advocate Mr. Hasurkar, the village Alampur was located adjoining the National Highway, whereas the same was not the case as regards the village in which the land in question was situated.

Learned Advocate Mr. Hasurkar would also submit that the appellant had produced a valuation report before the learned Reference Court,
wherein it had claimed the value of the land as Rs. 61 per sq. mtr. and yet, the learned Reference Court had fixed the value of the land at Rs. 100 per sq. mtr.

Learned Advocate Mr. Hasurkar would submit that on the above two counts, it clearly appears that the learned Reference Court had gravely erred and whereas for such reasons, learned Advocate Mr. Hasurkar would request this Court to interfere with the judgment and order passed by the learned Reference Court.
6. This appeal is vehemently contested by learned Advocate Mr. K.M. Sheth for the respondents - original claimants.

Learned Advocate would submit that as such, while it was the case of the appellant herein that the land situated at village Alampur, which is according to learned Advocate a comparable instance, was situated around 11 k.m. from the present land, yet, according to learned Advocate, the same had not been believed by the learned Reference Court.

Learned Advocate would further submit that the learned Reference Court had given cogent reasons for considering the land NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1719/2008 JUDGMENT DATED: 19/01/2023 undefined situated at Village Alampur as being comparable instance and whereas learned Advocate would submit that since the appellant herein - respondent in the Reference, had not produced any evidence disproving the evidence led by the claimants, therefore no fault could be found with the learned Reference Court in passing the impugned judgment and order.

Learned Advocate as regards the valuation would submit that while the valuation had been placed by the claimants themselves, whereas learned Advocate would submit that much reliance has not been placed by the learned Reference Court on the valuation, more particularly since according to learned Advocate, the learned Reference Court was concerned with the fact of the land situated at village Alampur, being a comparable instance, the learned Reference Court had fixed the rate of the present land as it was Executive Engineer (Constru.) vs Manguben Wd/O. 3 fixed for village Alampur.

sentences.text: Having regard to such submissions, learned Advocate Mr. Sheth would submit that the impugned judgment and order may not be interfered with by this Court.
7. Heard learned Advocates for the respective parties and perused the record and proceedings including a map which had been tendered at Exh. 35 by the present appellant.

The questions which arise for consideration of this Court being :
(i) Whether the judgment and decree passed by the learned NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1719/2008 JUDGMENT DATED: 19/01/2023 undefined Reference Court is required to be interfered with.
(ii) If yes, then what would be the relief to be granted.

7.2 My answers to the issues for consideration are as follows :
 (i) In affirmative.
 (ii) As per final order.
8.

At the outset, this Court seeks to rely upon the observations of the Hon'ble Apex Court in a recent decision in case of Somakka (Dead) By Legal Representatives vs K.P.Basavaraj (Dead) By Legal Repersentatives, reported in (2022) 8 SCC 261.

entities.text: Somakka (Dead) By Legal Representatives vs K.P.Basavaraj (Dead) By Legal Repersentatives, reported in (2022) 8 SCC 261
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Paragraph Nos. 30 to 32.4 of the said decision being relevant for the present purpose is quoted hereinbelow for benefit :

"30. It has been a matter of debate in a catena of decisions as to what would be the scope, power and duty of the first appellate court in deciding an appeal under Section 96 CPC read with Order 41 Rule 31 CPC.
We briefly deal with the law on the point.
31. The learned Judge V.R. Krishna Iyer, J., [as he then was a Judge of the Kerala High Court]

in 1969, while deciding the case between Kurian Chacko vs. Varkey Ouseph, dealing with a similar judgment of the first appellate court which had been disposed of by a brief order, observed as follows:
"2. An appellate court is the final court of fact ordinarily and therefore a litigant is entitled to a full and fair and independent NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1719/2008 JUDGMENT DATED: 19/01/2023 undefined consideration of the evidence at the appellate stage. Anything less than this is unjust to him and I have no doubt that in the present case the learned Subordinate Judge has fallen far short of what is expected of him as an appellate court."
32.

Further following the above, there have been a series of judgments by this Court:
Executive Engineer (Constru.) vs Manguben Wd/O. Maganbhai Ishwarbhai on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/16942560/
4 32.1

sentences.text: In Santosh Hazari vs. Purushottam Tiwari (relevant portion of para 15) is reproduced below:
"15...The appellate court has jurisdiction to reverse or affirm the findings of the Trial Court.
First appeal is a valuable right of the parties and unless restricted by law, the whole case is therein open for rehearing both on questions of fact and law.

The judgment of the appellate Court must, therefore, reflect if conscious application of mind and record findings supported by reasons, on all the issues arising along with the contentions put forth, and pressed by the parties for decision of the appellate court.

... while reversing a finding of fact the appellate court must come into close quarters with the reasoning assigned by the trial court and then assign its own reasons for arriving at a different finding.
This would satisfy the court hearing a further appeal that the first appellate court had discharged the duty expected of it."
32.2 In H.K.N. Swami vs. Irshad Basith, this Court again reiterated the same principle in para 3 of the judgment:
" 3. The first appeal has to be decided on facts as well as on law.

In the first appeal parties have the right to be heard both on questions of law as also on facts and the first appellate court is required to address itself to all issues and decide the case by giving reasons.
Unfortunately, the High Court, in the present case has not recorded any finding either on facts or on law.
Sitting as the first appellate court it was the duty of the High Court to deal with all the issues and the evidence led by the parties before recording the finding regarding title."
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1719/2008 JUDGMENT DATED: 19/01/2023 undefined 32.3

In 2015,
this Court again in Vinod Kumar vs. Gangadhar considering the previous judgment recorded its view in paras 18 and 19 which are reproduced hereunder:
"18.

In our considered opinion, the High Court did not deal with any of the submissions urged by the appellant and/or the respondent nor it took note of the grounds taken by the appellant in grounds of appeal nor made any attempt to appreciate the evidence adduced by the parties in the light of the settled legal principles and decided case law applicable to the issues arising in the case with a view to find out as to whether the judgment of the trial court can be sustained or not and if so, how, and if not, why.

19. Being the first appellate court, it was the duty of the High Court to have decided the first appeal keeping in view the scope and powers conferred on it under Section 96 read with Order 41 Rule 31 CPC mentioned above.

It was unfortunately not done,
thereby, resulting in causing prejudice to the appellant whose valuable right to prosecute in the first appeal on facts and law was adversely affected which, in turn,
deprived him of a hearing in the appeal in accordance with law.

It is for this reason,
we were unable to uphold the impugned judgment of the High Court."

sentences.text: Very recently, this Court in 2022 (to which one of us, Brother Abdul Nazeer, J. was a member)
in Manjual vs. Shyamsundar, reiterated the same view in para 8 thereof, which is reproduced hereunder:
"8. Section 96 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (for short "CPC") provides for filing of an appeal from the decree passed by a court of original jurisdiction.
Order 41 Rule 31 CPC provides the guidelines to the appellate court for deciding the appeal.
It is settled law
that an appeal is a continuation of the original proceedings
. The appellate court's jurisdiction involves a rehearing of appeal on questions of law as well as fact.
The first appeal is a valuable right, and, at that stage, all questions of fact and law decided by the trial court are open for reconsideration.

The judgment of the appellate court must, therefore, reflect conscious application of mind and must record the court's findings, supported by reasons for its decision in respect of all the issues, along with the contentions put forth and pressed by the parties.

Needless to say, the first appellate court is required to comply with the requirements of Order 41 Rule 31 CPC and non-observance of these requirements lead to infirmity in the judgment.""
8.1.

From the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court as hereinabove, more particularly after referring to various earlier decisions of the Hon'ble Apex Court,
being that an appeal is a continuation of the original proceedings, that the Appellate Court has jurisdiction to reverse or affirm the findings of the Trial Court, that the Appellate Court's jurisdiction involves a rehearing of appeal on questions of law as well as on fact.

Furthermore, as regards reversing of finding of fact, the Appellate Court is required to scrutinize the reasoning assigned by the Trial Court minutely and assign its own reasons for arriving at a different findings.

sentences.text: Since both the issues raised are co-relatable, the reasons for arriving at the conclusion would be discussed jointly hereinafter.

Issue Nos. 1 and 2 :
10.

While it was the contention of the appellant before the learned Reference Court that judgment and order with regard to Reference of village Alampur would not be applicable to the present case, since village Alampur is quite far away from the present village.
It was further the contention of the appellant herein, before the learned Reference Court that there were 04 villages situated between the village in question i.e. village Sadara and village Alampur.

It appears that the said contentions had not been considered by the learned Reference Court, more particularly by holding that the distance between villages Alampur and Sadara could not be more than 8 km.

Furthermore, according to the learned Reference Court, since the appellant herein had not produced any sale deed or judgment with regard to the villages between Sadara and Alampur, therefore also the aspect of there being 04 villages between village Sadara and village Alampur could not be considered.

Furthermore, the learned Reference Court has also inter alia observed that order with regard to land reference of village Alampur would be held as comparable instance as regards village Sadara, since outskirts of both the villages were adjacent to each other.

NEU  C/FA/1719/2008 JUDGMENT DATED: 19/01/2023  und Executive Engineer (Constru.) vs Manguben Wd/O. Maganbhai Ishwarbhai on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/16942560/
7 11.

sentences.text:
From the evidence led by the appellant, it appears that the appellant herein had by way of Exh.
35 produced a map of Gandhinagar District to contend that the villages in question were far from each other and whereas from a perusal of the map it would appear that villages Sadara and Alampur, are situated at quite some distance from each other.
It also clearly appears that there were lands of four villages situated between villages Alampur and Sadara.
Most importantly it appears that village Alampur is situated adjacent to National Highway No. 8-C.

That National Highway No.
8-C is situated on the southern side of village Alampur and whereas village Sadara is situated on the northern side of village Alampur.

It would also be pertinent to mention that National Highway No.8 is located on the eastern side of village Sadara again at some distance and whereas there is no exact detail as to the distance between National Highway No.8 and village Sadara.

From the map, it clearly appears that village Sadara and village Alampur could not be termed as adjacent villages by any stretch of imagination and whereas villages Sadara and Alampur were situated at considerable distance from each other.

12. It further appears that the said aspect of village Sadara and Alampur being at a distance from each other and that around four villages located between the villages Sadara and Alampur, had been stated by witness of the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1719/2008 JUDGMENT DATED: 19/01/2023 undefined appellant herein before the learned Reference Court and whereas it does not appear that he had been subjected to any cross-examination on such aspect.

13. Thus, it appears that while ample material had been produced by the appellant herein as regards land of village Sadara and village Alampur not being comparable instance and the witness of the appellant herein had also deposed as regards the same and inspite of the witness not being subjected to cross-examination on the said issue and the respondents herein - claimants not having led any evidence to disprove the same, yet the learned Reference Court had arrived at finding that the land situated at village Sadara i.e. the acquired land and the land situated at village Alampur i.e.
compared land were adjacent lands.
Thus, it would appear that the finding of fact by the learned Reference Court on the above count requires interference.

14. Furthermore, it also requires to be mentioned here that the impugned judgment and order also requires interference on account of the fact that the claimants themselves had produced evidence showing that the valuation of the land in the year 1992 would be Rs. 61/- per sq. mtr., more particularly Notification under Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act was published in the year 1992.

It appears that inspite thereof, only on the fact of the land NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1719/2008 JUDGMENT DATED: 19/01/2023 undefined situated at village Alampur being a comparable instance and the claimants having calculated the market value of the land based upon the same,
therefore the learned Reference Court had brushed a side the same.
15. Perusal of the valuation report produced by the claimants at Exh. 27 reveals that the valuer had valued the land at Rs. 61/- per sq. mtr. as on 31.12.1991.

The claimants themselves having led evidence with regard to value of the land as being Rs. 61/-, in the considered opinion of this Court,
the learned Reference Court ought not to have fixed the value of the land at Rs. 100/- per sq. mtr.,

8 more particularly based upon erroneous finding of fact.

sentences.text: 16. Having arrived at a conclusion as above that the impugned judgment and order requires interference, since evidence had been led by the claimants as regards the value of the land in the year 1992 i.e. the year in which Section 4 Notification was issued and the appellant herein had not led any evidence to the contrary and since the acquisition proceedings have commenced more than 03 decades earlier and since as per the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in case of Somakka (supra) the First Appellate Court is empowered to vary or modify the findings of the learned Trial Court

and since the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in an appeal NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1719/2008 JUDGMENT DATED: 19/01/2023 undefined under Section 96 read with Order 41 Rule 31 of the Civil Procedure Code, would also be applicable mutatis mutandis in an appeal under Section 54 of the Land Acquisition Act
, in the considered opinion of this Court, this Court deems it appropriate not to remand the reference for fresh consideration.

17. Having regard to the above discussion, in the considered opinion of this Court, the impugned judgment and order dated 14.02.2007 passed by the learned Principal Senior Civil Judge,
Gandhinagar, in Land Acquisition Reference No. 575 of 1998, is interfered with to the extent of fixing the additional compensation payable to the claimants at the rate of Rs. 57/- per sq. mtr. (i.e.
taking the value of the land at Rs. 61 per sq. mtr. as per the valuation report of the claimant less the amount awarded i.e. Rs. 4 per sq. mtr.) over and above the amount of compensation already awarded by the Special Land Acquisition Officer for the acquired lands.

Rest of the directions including payment of additional amount of compensation at the rate of 12% on additional compensation awarded to claimants as per the provisions of Section 23 (1-A) of the Land Acquisition Act, payment of solatium at the rate of 30% on the additional amount of compensation under Section 23(2) of the Land Acquisition Act and payment of interest on the additional compensation at the rate of 9% per annum from the date of NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1719/2008 JUDGMENT DATED: 19/01/2023 undefined taking over the possession or from the date of issuance of Notification under Section 4 of the Act, whichever is earlier for the first year and thereafter, at the rate of 15% per annum till realization of the payable aggregate amount according to the provisions of Section 28 of the Land Acquisition Act, are not interfered with.
18. Decree be drawn accordingly.
19. The present first appeal stands disposed of as partly allowed on the above terms.
Record and Proceedings to be transmitted back to the Reference Court.
